text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm about to open a small Terraform PR that tightens cluster autoscaling constraints and adds a Karpenter provisioner limit. Want a quick sanity check before I land it. 

maria: TL;DR changes: reduce GKE node_pool max_nodes from 200 -> 100, and add a `limits.resources` stanza to the karpenter provisioner to cap burst CPU. Planning a canary rollout to Dedicated first.

maria: Terraform diff (excerpt):
```hcl
resource "google_container_node_pool" "default" {
  name      = "worker-pool"
  max_nodes = 100 # was 200
  autoscaling {
    max_node_count = 100
    min_node_count = 3
  }
}
```

maria: Karpenter provisioner snippet I'm adding:
```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: "4000" # caps total CPU across provisioner
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 259200
```

maria: Specific asks: 
- Any workloads that routinely scale past 100 nodes?
- HPA/VPA interactions we should be careful of?
- Secrets or provider credentials that would break if new nodes come up slower?

jon: @maria I don't think we have anything that needs >100 nodes, but a few batch jobs spin up many pods on short windows. Are those using PodDisruptionBudgets or batch queues? :eyes:

ashwin: For the batch stuff — they use a Job-based controller and a short-lived autoscaled replica count; they usually rely on CA to spin nodes quickly. If node creation gets throttled this could queue pods. Recommend setting `spec.consolidation=false` temporarily for those provisioners during canary.

jon: Also check HPAs that target average CPU across pods — if nodes get denser, HPA targetPercent might overshoot and cause more evictions. Look for any HPA with `targetAverageUtilization: >= 80`.

lee: Quick query you can run to find potentially risky deployments: 
```bash
kubectl get deploy --all-namespaces -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}	{.metadata.name}	{.spec.replicas}
{end}' | sort -k3 -n | tail -n 30
```

ashwin: To find HPAs with high thresholds: 
```bash
kubectl get hpa --all-namespaces -o yaml | yq '.items[] | select(.spec.metrics[].resource.target.averageUtilization >= 80) | {namespace: .metadata.namespace, name: .metadata.name, target: .spec.metrics}'
```

maria: Thanks — I'll run those queries and flag any offending services. If we find batch jobs that could block, we can set a pod priority or move them to a different nodeSelector during the rollout.

infra-bot: CI: terraform plan for PR #4521 succeeded — no destructive changes expected. Plan: add node_pool.max_nodes -> 100. Pipelines: https://ci.redwood.example/pipelines/4521 :white_check_mark:

jon: One more note — VPA mode for a few statefulsets is `Auto` which can trigger restarts when recommendations apply. Might be safer to switch those to `Off` or `Initial` during the change window.

maria: Good call. I'll set VPA for known stateful services to `Initial` in the canary cluster and record them in the PR description.

lee: Also check cluster-autoscaler configmap `--scale-down-unneeded-time` and `--max-node-provision-time` values. If you reduce max nodes, scale-down aggressiveness can cause churn.

maria: I'll hold the PR until I run the queries and update the PR with the list of adjusted HPAs/VPAs and a rollout plan (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Planning to monitor pod pending time and API server throttles.

jon: Ping me when ready; I can shepherd the canary on Dedicated.

maria: Thanks all — will post the PR link in this thread when it's up. :thumbsup:
